This is #1871/#1877's "library models are the moat" thesis showing up as a scoreboard number. It's also the one item with a real false-green hazard — an authored-complete request summary is the first place Bifrost could clear a vulnerable case — so the experiment must gate on false-greens-stay-0 before anything ships as default.
2. **#2355 is the cheapest 20% you'll ever buy** — the bakeoff's own sink/source sets miss `JdbcTemplate` and friends. Worth doing before #2354 so the summary experiment measures against a corpus that can actually bind.

Until then the differentiator is asserted, not demonstrated.
4. Items that fell off the list: budget/charging work (all walls down, six of them), CHA expansion (measured null twice — cheap to re-test, wrong to invest in now), and everything in the residual chain (empty).

Rough sequencing that maximizes slope: #2355 → #2354 experiment (false-green-gated) → re-run bakeoff + #2277 A/B + #1871 sweep in one session → then decide between #2276 and the honest-completion plumbing with fresh numbers.
